discovery: Quantum simulation of many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Juan Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Zoller and Cirac showed theoretically (Jaksch et al., 1998) that cold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model with fully controllable parameters, and laid the conceptual foundations for analog quantum simulation and for quantum information processing with atoms and ions. Bloch's 2002 observation of the superfluid-Mott insulator transition turned this proposal into a new field, followed by quantum gas microscopy, many-body localisation, artificial gauge fields and out-of-equilibrium dynamics studied with single-site resolution. Together they realised Feynman's vision of a quantum simulator: controllable quantum systems that solve problems intractable for classical computers. Their work unites quantum optics, condensed-matter physics and quantum information, and is used by hundreds of laboratories worldwide. It is a prime example of theory and experiment advancing hand in hand, and it underpins today's quantum technologies with neutral atoms.
